name: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
summary: Saint-Exupéry was an aristocratic-born airmail pilot and author who wrote little programmatic politics. In Flight to Arras he defends the primacy of Man and a universal civilization over the particular, rejecting both sameness-equality and individual licence, and opposed Nazi Germany, fighting until his death in 1944.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: He flew reconnaissance missions in the 1940 campaign and volunteered again in 1943-44 to fight alongside the Allies against German-occupied France.

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Describing the bombardment of Madrid, he says he cares nothing for the rules of war and reprisal and cannot see what military role the killing of housewives and children plays.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: In his credo (section XXVII of Pilote de guerre) he states belief in the equality of the rights of Man through each individual, adding that equality is not identity.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He argues that material equality, if defined and enforced, would require everyone to occupy an identical place and role, which he calls absurd: equality is not identity.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He rebuts the moralists who denounce the mechanical civilization as the enemy of the spirit, calling the machine a tool that brings people together, though he concedes some loss of craft and creative instinct (Wind, Sand and Stars).

resist-oppression-despite-death.rationale: He returned to combat flying in 1943 despite age and injuries and died on a mission;

shared-human-nature.rationale: He founds the only meaningful equality and liberty on the primacy of Man (a shared human essence) over the individual.

universal-morality.rationale: His credo holds that the cult of the Universal over the particular founds the only true order, and he vows to fight anyone imposing one custom, people, race or thought on others.

notes: Searched: Pilote de guerre full text (democracy, equality, liberty, civilization, war), Britannica, NEH. Political record otherwise thin; economy, government and most society themes have no stated position.
